content.text: Jaflong Zero Point is a famous tourist attraction because this is where the River Dawki crosses India and enters into Bangladesh. Situated on a high altitude this viewpoint overlooks the Dawki river. Most tourists visit this place as it marks the Indo Bangladesh border, which is marked by a huge rock on the dry river bed. a place where you can meet tourists both from India and Bangladesh, it’s a very unique experience accompanied by the thrill-seeking view. Jaflong is famous for being home to the Khasi Tribes and for the stones present there. The smiles across the border will definitely make your day.

One of the cleanest rivers in Asia, the Umngot River also known as the Dawki River flows through the Jainita Valley and Khasi Hills eventually flowing into Bangladesh. Being a major tourist attraction this river has been going viral due to its clear water. Tourists are eager to go boating in this emerald green water. Travellers have shared that boating in this river is a whole new experience and it feels like they are flying over the water body. The rocks and the swimming fishes can be witnessed with your naked eye. The natives suggest that it is ideal to visit this place on a sunny day as the water becomes more clear and visible.

Located on the banks of river Umngot, this small village is the epitome of thrilling adventures. To explore the beauty of this place you can reside at the comfortable and heart-warming homestays offered by the locals. Every year during the months of February – April annual water sports festival takes place. You can go for
Camping at Shnongpdeng, Dawki
and also check out the water activities such as kayaking, boat rides, and so on. The abundance of the dense forest makes it ideal for trekking and camping.

Borhill Falls is located between Dawki and Lyngkha and is one of the lesser known places of Dawki. The Bangladesh plains can be seen from there. Unfortunately, it is a hidden gem of Meghalaya that has mesmerizing views similar to the other waterfalls. This unexplored beauty is a must-visit destination near Dawki. This waterfall shows you how serene and magnificent nature can be. The ambiance of this place is so special that you may not want to leave the place.

One of the heritage structures built during the British era is the Dawki Suspension Bridge built-in 1932. this bridge is a major connection between East Khasi Hills and West Jaintia Hills. This bridge built over the Umngot River is a major lifeline connection for the locals of the Riwar area.

This living root bridge connects two small cliffs, making it a unique tourist attraction. It is unbelievable to see that this man-made bridge made from roots has been sustained for so many years by the locals. Formed out of intertwined roots that cross over a stream will give you a different kind of experience. This bridge can be accessed by all and will take a small fraction of time to cover. The experience of standing treetops will be worth while, you can also get a closer experience of how the locals lead their lives.

The travel time from Shillong to Dawki via NH206 is 2 hours 47 minutes. Usually travellers do not stop while travelling from Shillong to Dawki. However, if you want to stop for tea-sipping on the local restaurants or for taking photos, you can do that.
